title: Independent predictors of time from symptom onset to discharge among patients with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome: a retrospective cohort study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is a tick-borne bunyaviral infection with heterogeneous recovery trajectories and high case fatality. Most prior studies use in-hospital mortality as the primary endpoint; few quantify independent predictors of recovery duration among surviving patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We performed a retrospective cohort analysis of 43 consecutive laboratory-confirmed SFTS survivors discharged from Taizhou Hospital of Zhejiang Province (July 2019–April 2025).
analysis.methods: Demographics, laboratory values, and organ involvement data were extracted from electronic medical records. Univariate correlation and group comparisons screened candidate variables; backward stepwise multiple linear regression was applied to identify independent predictors after multicollinearity diagnosis via variance inflation factor (VIF).
analysis.main_results: The mean total recovery duration was 16.58 ± 7.86 days. Univariate analysis demonstrated significant correlations between longer discharge time and three variables: prolonged platelet decline duration (r=0.6577, P<0.0001), delayed hospital admission after symptom onset (r=0.7441, P<0.0001), and presence of cardiac/circulatory involvement (P = 0.0002).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Multivariate regression confirmed three independent predictors: platelet decline duration (β=0.63, P = 0.0001), cardiac/circulatory involvement (β=5.33, P = 0.0003), and days from onset to hospitalization (β=1.41, P<0.001).
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Dynamic monitoring of platelet counts and cardiovascular biomarkers enables risk stratification. Early hospital presentation, targeted platelet support, and cardioprotective management may shorten disease courses and optimize medical resource utilization for SFTS patients.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The final model had an adjusted R 2 of 0.7762, explaining 77.62% of variance in recovery time; all included variables had VIF<2.5 without severe multicollinearity. All statistical tests were two-sided (α=0.05).

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to identify clinical and laboratory factors independently associated with recovery duration among patients with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS). A retrospective cohort analysis of 43 laboratory-confirmed SFTS survivors was conducted at Taizhou Hospital of Zhejiang Province between July 2019 and April 2025. Data on demographics, laboratory values, and organ involvement were extracted from electronic medical records. Univariate correlation and group comparisons were used to screen candidate variables, followed by backward stepwise multiple linear regression to identify independent predictors after multicollinearity diagnosis via variance inflation factor (VIF). The mean total recovery duration was 16.58 ± 7.86 days. Univariate analysis showed significant correlations between longer discharge time and prolonged platelet decline duration (r=0.6577, P<0.0001), delayed hospital admission after symptom onset (r=0.7441, P<0.0001), and presence of cardiac/circulatory involvement (P = 0.0002). Multivariate regression confirmed three independent predictors: platelet decline duration (β=0.63, P = 0.0001), cardiac/circulatory involvement (β=5.33, P = 0.0003), and days from onset to hospitalization (β=1.41, P<0.001). The final model had an adjusted R 2 of 0.7762, explaining 77.62% of variance in recovery time, with all included variables having VIF<2.5. The authors concluded that prolonged platelet decline duration, cardiovascular organ injury, and delayed hospital admission after symptom onset independently prolong hospitalization duration among discharged SFTS survivors.

title: Neighbor-associated components in endemic–epidemic surveillance models: scrub typhus, Japanese spotted fever and severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome in Japan as a biological negative-control setting, 2013–2025

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate how different baseline risk specifications affect the estimation of neighbor-associated components in endemic–epidemic surveillance models, using severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome as a biological negative-control setting.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed weekly notifications of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome across 47 Japanese prefectures from 2013 to 2025, fitting negative-binomial endemic–epidemic models under five area-baseline specifications.
analysis.methods: Negative-binomial endemic–epidemic models were fitted under five area-baseline specifications, ranging from a single national intercept to prefecture-specific effects, using aggregated national surveillance data.
analysis.main_results: Under a single national intercept, the neighbor-associated fraction for severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome was 0.149 (95% confidence interval 0.120–0.180), which fell to below 0.002 under prefecture-specific baselines.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings show that the estimated neighbor-associated fraction is highly dependent on the baseline risk specification, and that genuine coupling can only be recovered when the fitted spatial operator aligns with the generating one.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results highlight the importance of carefully specifying baseline risk and spatial weights in surveillance models to avoid misinterpreting statistical dependence as actual transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's results are limited by the use of aggregated data and the assumption that spatial operators are correctly aligned, with moderate confidence due to the absence of direct transmission evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how different baseline risk specifications influence the estimation of neighbor-associated components in endemic–epidemic surveillance models, using severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome as a negative-control setting. The analysis of weekly notifications across 47 Japanese prefectures from 2013 to 2025 revealed that the neighbor-associated fraction varied significantly depending on the model structure. Under a single national intercept, the fraction was 0.149 (95% CI 0.120–0.180), but it dropped to below 0.002 with prefecture-specific baselines. The authors emphasize that these fractions are specification-dependent summaries of statistical dependence and should not be interpreted as direct transmission without independent corroboration. The study's findings underscore the need for careful model design in surveillance to avoid misinterpretation of spatial associations. However, the results are limited by the use of aggregated data and the assumption of correct spatial operator alignment, which may affect the strength of the evidence.

title: Co-infection with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus and Rickettsia monacensis in Korea

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the prevalence of co-infection with Rickettsia monacensis in patients with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) in Korea, as co-infections between SFTSV and R. monacensis remain poorly characterized despite their shared ecological niches.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in Korea between 2024 and 2026, analyzing clinical samples from 129 patients diagnosed with SFTS. The focus was on identifying co-infections with Rickettsia monacensis in these patients.
analysis.methods: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and sequencing were used to detect SFTSV and Rickettsia monacensis. One-step reverse-transcription PCR was performed for SFTSV, while rickettsial nested PCR targeting outer membrane protein A (ompA) was used for R.
analysis.main_results: Among the 129 SFTS cases, nine patients were found to be co-infected with Rickettsia monacensis, resulting in a prevalence rate of 7.9%. Phylogenetic analysis showed that the seven sequences identified clustered closely with R.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate that co-infection with Rickettsia monacensis is a notable occurrence in SFTS patients in Korea, highlighting the need for further investigation into the clinical implications of such co-infections.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results emphasize the importance of considering co-infections in the differential diagnosis of tick-borne febrile illnesses and may inform improved diagnostic and management strategies for SFTS in Korea.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on molecular testing and the potential for false negatives, but the prevalence rate of 7.9% is based on direct testing of clinical samples, providing moderate confidence in the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the prevalence of Rickettsia monacensis co-infection in patients with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) in Korea. Using PCR and sequencing, clinical samples from 129 SFTS patients were analyzed, revealing that 7.9% were co-infected with R. monacensis. Phylogenetic analysis showed that the sequences clustered closely with R. monacensis. The findings highlight the need for differential diagnosis of tick-borne febrile illnesses and raise awareness of the potential impacts of co-infections on disease severity and management. The study provides moderate confidence in its results, though it is limited by its reliance on molecular testing and the possibility of false negatives.
